l: Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, Abstract
s: The text concerns large language models (LMs), which can understand and generate language but often produce factually inaccurate output. It describes retrieval augmented LMs that use external knowledge resources, noting that most retrieve information only once from the input. The work presents active retrieval augmented generation and proposes Forward-Looking Active REtrieval augmented generation (FLARE), which repeatedly predicts upcoming sentences, retrieves relevant documents, and regenerates sentences containing low-confidence tokens. FLARE achieves superior or competitive performance across four long-form knowledge-intensive generation tasks/datasets.

l: language model, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, Abstract
s: Large language models have a remarkable ability to comprehend and generate language, but they tend to hallucinate and produce factually inaccurate output.

l: hallucination, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, Abstract
s: Hallucination is identified as a tendency of large language models to create factually inaccurate output.

l: external knowledge resources, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, Abstract
s: External knowledge resources are used to augment language models and are presented as one promising solution to hallucination and factual inaccuracy.

l: retrieval augmented LMs, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, Abstract
s: Retrieval augmented LMs retrieve information from external knowledge resources to support generation. Most existing retrieval augmented LMs use a retrieve-and-generate setup that retrieves information only once based on the input, which limits them in longer generation scenarios.

l: active retrieval augmented generation, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, Abstract
s: Active retrieval augmented generation is described as a generalized approach in which methods actively decide when and what to retrieve throughout the course of generation.

l: FLARE, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, Abstract
s: Forward-Looking Active REtrieval augmented generation (FLARE) iteratively predicts the upcoming sentence and uses that prediction as a query to retrieve relevant documents. It regenerates the sentence when it contains low-confidence tokens and achieves superior or competitive performance across four long-form knowledge-intensive generation tasks/datasets.

l: long-form knowledge-intensive generation tasks/datasets, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, Abstract
s: FLARE and baseline methods are evaluated comprehensively on four long-form knowledge-intensive generation tasks/datasets. FLARE achieves superior or competitive performance on all of them.

l: Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, Introduction
s: The unit concerns generative language models and the challenge of hallucination, proposing retrieval during generation to provide needed external knowledge. It introduces Forward-Looking Active REtrieval augmented generation (FLARE), which generates a temporary future sentence, retrieves documents when that sentence contains low-probability tokens, and regenerates it using the retrieved information. FLARE is designed for long-form tasks and can be applied to existing language models at inference time without additional training. Evaluations using text-davinci-003 on four datasets found that FLARE achieved superior or competitive performance against single-time and multi-time retrieval baselines.

l: language model, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, Introduction
s: Generative language models have become foundational components in natural language processing systems and have demonstrated abilities in long-form question answering, open-domain summarization, and chain-of-thought reasoning. Although they memorize some world knowledge during training, they still tend to hallucinate.

l: hallucination, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, Introduction
s: Hallucination is the creation of imaginary content by language models. Retrieval components that consult external knowledge resources are presented as a promising way to address it.

l: retrieval augmented LMs, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, Introduction
s: Retrieval augmented language models commonly retrieve documents from a user's input and generate an answer conditioned on those documents. Single-time retrieval is effective for short-form knowledge-intensive tasks when the information needs are clear in the input, but complex long-form generation may require additional retrieval during generation.

l: long-form generation, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, Introduction
s: Long-form generation involves complex information needs that are not always evident from the input alone. It may require gathering multiple pieces of knowledge throughout generation, as in long-form question answering, open-domain summarization, and chain-of-thought reasoning.

l: active retrieval, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, Introduction
s: Active retrieval retrieves information only when a language model generates low-probability tokens, based on the hypothesis that low confidence often indicates a lack of knowledge. It also considers what the model intends to generate in the future by using a temporary next sentence as a retrieval query.

l: FLARE, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, Introduction
s: Forward-Looking Active REtrieval augmented generation (FLARE) iteratively generates a temporary next sentence, checks whether it contains low-probability tokens, retrieves relevant documents when needed, and regenerates the sentence using those documents. It applies at inference time to existing language models without additional training and is evaluated on multihop question answering, commonsense reasoning, long-form question answering, and open-domain summarization.

l: GPT-3.5, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, Introduction
s: GPT-3.5 is identified as achieving impressive performance across a variety of tasks. Its effectiveness is examined through the use of text-davinci-003.

l: text-davinci-003, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, Introduction
s: text-davinci-003 is used to examine the effectiveness of FLARE. Across four long-output tasks, FLARE achieves superior or competitive performance compared with single-time and multi-time retrieval baselines.

l: Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 2 .. 2.3
s: The unit defines Retrieval Augmented Generation for producing answers from a user input and a document corpus. It explains that a retriever returns documents for a query and that a language model conditions on the user input and retrieved documents. Single-time retrieval augmented generation retrieves once using the user input and generates the complete answer. Active retrieval augmented generation interleaves retrieval and generation by formulating queries from the user input and previously generated output, while retaining only the current retrieval results as context.

l: Retrieval Augmented Generation, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 2 .. 2.3
s: Retrieval Augmented Generation generates answers by leveraging information retrieved from a document corpus. It includes single-time retrieval augmented generation and active retrieval augmented generation.

l: Single-time ret., Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 2 .. 2.3
s: Single-time retrieval augmented generation uses the user input directly as the retrieval query and generates the complete answer at once.

l: active retrieval augmented generation, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 2 .. 2.3
s: Active retrieval augmented generation actively decides when and what to retrieve throughout the generation process. It interleaves retrieval and generation, formulates queries from the user input and previously generated output, and uses only the documents retrieved at the current step.

l: user input, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 2 .. 2.3
s: The user input is combined with retrieved documents to condition answer generation. It serves as the initial query for active retrieval augmented generation and is directly used as the query in single-time retrieval augmented generation.

l: document corpus, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 2 .. 2.3
s: The document corpus contains documents from which information is retrieved to help generate an answer.

l: retriever, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 2 .. 2.3
s: The retriever retrieves a list of documents for a query.

l: language model, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 2 .. 2.3
s: The language model conditions on the user input and retrieved documents to generate the answer. In active retrieval augmented generation, it continually generates tokens using the current retrieved documents, the user input, and previous generation.

l: query, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 2 .. 2.3
s: A query is used by the retriever to obtain a list of documents. In active retrieval augmented generation, the query is formulated from the user input and previously generated output.

l: retrieved documents, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 2 .. 2.3
s: Retrieved documents are prepended before the user input to support future generation. In active retrieval augmented generation, previously retrieved documents are discarded so that only the current retrieved documents condition the next generation.

l: answer, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 2 .. 2.3
s: The answer is generated as a sequence of sentences or tokens by leveraging information retrieved from the document corpus.

l: long-form generation, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 2 .. 2.3
s: The generation process in active retrieval augmented generation interleaves retrieval with continued answer generation. Retrieval is triggered during generation until the answer reaches its end.

l: Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 3 .. 3.3
s: Forward-Looking Active REtrieval Augmented Generation (FLARE) is a framework for active retrieval augmented generation that retrieves information when the language model lacks necessary knowledge and forms queries around future generation needs. It introduces FLAREinstruct, which uses retrieval instructions to prompt search queries during answer generation, and FLAREdirect, which uses the model’s provisional next sentence to decide whether and what to retrieve. FLAREdirect triggers retrieval when any token in the temporary next sentence has probability below a threshold, then regenerates the sentence using retrieved documents. The unit describes masked-sentence and generated-question approaches for formulating retrieval queries and reports an implementation using GPT-3.5, BM25, and Bing.

l: FLARE, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 3 .. 3.3
s: Forward-Looking Active REtrieval Augmented Generation (FLARE) is proposed as a framework that retrieves information only when needed and makes retrieval queries reflect the intents of future generations. It includes FLAREinstruct and FLAREdirect.

l: active retrieval augmented generation, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 3 .. 3.3
s: Active retrieval augmented generation is the framework implemented by FLARE methods. It is intended to avoid unnecessary or inappropriate retrieval while accessing information when the language model lacks necessary knowledge.

l: FLAREinstruct, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 3 .. 3.3
s: FLAREinstruct prompts the language model to generate search queries when additional information is needed while it generates an answer. When a search query is generated, the system retrieves relevant documents and prepends them before the user input to support future generation.

l: FLAREdirect, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 3 .. 3.3
s: FLAREdirect uses the language model’s generation as search queries and iteratively generates the next sentence to assess the future topic. If the provisional sentence contains uncertain tokens, it retrieves relevant documents and regenerates the sentence.

l: language model, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 3 .. 3.3
s: The language model generates answers, retrieval queries, and temporary next sentences in the FLARE methods. Its token probabilities are used to estimate confidence, and low confidence can trigger retrieval.

l: retrieval instructions, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 3 .. 3.3
s: Retrieval instructions guide language models to generate search queries such as '[Search(query)]' when additional information is needed. FLAREinstruct combines these instructions with downstream-task instructions and exemplars.

l: confidence-based active retrieval, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 3 .. 3.3
s: Confidence-based active retrieval first generates a temporary next sentence without retrieved documents. It accepts the sentence when all token probabilities meet the threshold and otherwise retrieves documents before regenerating it.

l: confidence-based query formulation, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 3 .. 3.3
s: Confidence-based query formulation creates queries from the temporary next sentence when low-confidence tokens trigger retrieval. It can mask low-confidence tokens or generate explicit questions targeting uncertain spans.

l: query, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 3 .. 3.3
s: A retrieval query can be generated through retrieval instructions, taken directly from the temporary next sentence, formed by masking low-confidence tokens, or produced as a question about an uncertain span. The queries are used to retrieve documents that aid future generation.

l: retrieval, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 3 .. 3.3
s: Retrieval is triggered when the language model lacks confidence in part of a temporary next sentence or explicitly generates a search request. Retrieved documents are supplied to the language model to support subsequent or regenerated text.

l: upcoming sentence, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 3 .. 3.3
s: The temporary next sentence is generated without conditioning on retrieved documents and is used to assess confidence and formulate queries. If it contains a token below the confidence threshold, it can be replaced by a regenerated sentence based on retrieved documents.

l: GPT-3.5, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 3 .. 3.3
s: GPT-3.5 models are used for the described implementation, including text-davinci-003 for iterative API querying. GPT-3.5-turbo is also prompted to generate questions targeting low-confidence spans.

l: Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 4
s: The section on Multi-time Retrieval Baselines formulates existing passive multi-time retrieval augmented LMs within the authors' framework. It introduces three baseline categories based on when and what to retrieve: Previous-window approaches, Previous-sentence approaches, and Question decomposition approaches. Previous-window approaches retrieve every fixed number of tokens, Previous-sentence approaches retrieve once per sentence, and Question decomposition approaches retrieve when a generated sub-question appears. The section notes that these approaches may use unsuitable queries, retrieve inefficiently, or require task-specific prompt engineering.

l: Multi-time Retrieval Baselines, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 4
s: Multi-time Retrieval Baselines formally introduce three categories of passive retrieval methods based on when and what they retrieve. They are implemented with the same settings while varying only the retrieval timing and content.

l: passive multi-time retrieval augmented LMs, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 4
s: Passive multi-time retrieval augmented LMs can be formulated using the framework described in subsection 2.3. Their baseline implementations differ in when and what they retrieve.

l: three baseline categories, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 4
s: The three baseline categories are Previous-window approaches, Previous-sentence approaches, and Question decomposition approaches.

l: Previous-window approaches, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 4
s: Previous-window approaches trigger retrieval every l tokens, using the generated tokens from the previous window as the query. The section follows Ram et al. (2023) in using a window size of l = 16.

l: Previous-sentence approaches, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 4
s: Previous-sentence approaches trigger retrieval every sentence and use the previous sentence as the query.

l: Question decomposition approaches, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 4
s: Question decomposition approaches use manually annotated, task-specific exemplars to guide LMs in generating decomposed sub-questions. Retrieval is triggered dynamically whenever the model generates a sub-question.

l: RETRO, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 4
s: RETRO is identified as an existing method in the Previous-window category and retrieves every few tokens.

l: IC-RALM, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 4
s: IC-RALM is identified as an existing method in the Previous-window category and retrieves every few tokens.

l: KNN-LM, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 4
s: KNN-LM is identified as an existing method in the Previous-window category and retrieves every token.

l: IRCoT, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 4
s: IRCoT is identified as a method in the Previous-sentence category, which triggers retrieval every sentence and uses the previous sentence as the query.

l: Self-ask, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 4
s: Self-ask is identified as a Question decomposition method. It manually inserts sub-questions in exemplars using Prompt D.2, and retrieval is triggered when the model generates a sub-question.

l: retrieval, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 4
s: Retrieval can occur every fixed number of tokens, every sentence, or dynamically when a sub-question is generated. The section notes that retrieval may be inefficient when performed at inappropriate points.

l: language model, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 4
s: The language model may use previously generated tokens as retrieval queries, although such queries might not reflect what it intends to generate in the future.

l: Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 5 .. Open-domain summarization
s: The unit describes the experimental setup for evaluating FLARE on knowledge-intensive tasks using few-shot in-context learning and up to 500 examples per dataset. It covers multihop QA with 2WikiMultihopQA, commonsense reasoning with StrategyQA, long-form QA with ASQA and ASQA-hint, and open-domain summarization with WikiAsp. The evaluation uses task-specific metrics, including exact match, token-level scores, Disambig-F1, ROUGE, DR, named entity-based F1, and UniEval. FLARE is compared with no retrieval, single-time retrieval, and previous-window retrieval across the datasets.

l: FLARE, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 5 .. Open-domain summarization
s: FLARE is evaluated on diverse knowledge-intensive tasks using few-shot in-context learning, with at most 500 examples sampled from each dataset. Its hyperparameters are selected on development sets, and FLAREdirect is used when FLARE is not otherwise specified.

l: 2WikiMultihopQA, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 5 .. Open-domain summarization
s: 2WikiMultihopQA is used to evaluate multihop QA with two-hop questions from Wikipedia that require composition, comparison, or inference. Outputs include a chain of thought and final answer, which are evaluated using exact match, token-level F1, precision, and recall.

l: multihop question answering, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 5 .. Open-domain summarization
s: Multihop QA involves answering complex questions through information retrieval and reasoning. The evaluation follows a setting that generates both chain-of-thought reasoning and a final answer.

l: StrategyQA, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 5 .. Open-domain summarization
s: StrategyQA is used to evaluate commonsense reasoning through crowdsourced yes/no questions. The system generates both a chain of thought and a final answer, and the extracted answer is compared with the gold answer using exact match.

l: commonsense reasoning, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 5 .. Open-domain summarization
s: Commonsense reasoning requires world and commonsense knowledge to generate answers. It is evaluated with StrategyQA using yes/no questions and exact-match scoring.

l: ASQA, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 5 .. Open-domain summarization
s: ASQA is used as a testbed for long-form QA involving ambiguous questions with multiple interpretations. Its outputs should address all interpretations and are evaluated with EM, Disambig-F1, ROUGE, and DR.

l: ASQA-hint, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 5 .. Open-domain summarization
s: ASQA-hint is a setting in which a brief hint is provided to guide language models when generating answers to ambiguous questions. It uses the same long-form QA metrics described for ASQA.

l: long-form question answering, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 5 .. Open-domain summarization
s: Long-form QA aims to generate comprehensive answers to questions seeking complex information. The unit evaluates it with ASQA and ASQA-hint, including metrics for disambiguation, question answering, overlap, and combined performance.

l: WikiAsp, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 5 .. Open-domain summarization
s: WikiAsp is used to evaluate open-domain summarization by generating aspect-based summaries about entities from 20 Wikipedia domains. Its metrics include ROUGE, named entity-based F1, and UniEval, which measures factual consistency.

l: open-domain summarization, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 5 .. Open-domain summarization
s: Open-domain summarization aims to generate a comprehensive summary about a topic by gathering information from the open web. The unit evaluates this task with WikiAsp.

l: Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 6 .. 6.2
s: This unit reports experimental results for FLARE across 2WikiMultihopQA, StrategyQA, ASQA, ASQA-hint, and WikiAsp, comparing it with single-time retrieval and several multi-time retrieval baselines. FLARE outperforms the baselines across the reported tasks and datasets, with especially strong gains on 2WikiMultihopQA. Ablations show that forward-looking retrieval using the next sentence is more effective than retrieval based on previous context, while active retrieval performs best when applied selectively. The results also show that implicit masking-based and explicit question-generation query formulation achieve similar performance.

l: FLARE, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 6 .. 6.2
s: FLARE outperforms all evaluated baselines across the reported tasks and datasets. Its direct variant reaches 51.0 EM and 59.7 F1 on 2WikiMultihopQA, and the method performs best overall on StrategyQA, ASQA, ASQA-hint, and WikiAsp. Its retrieval is most effective when activated selectively, and both implicit and explicit query formulation methods perform similarly.

l: baseline methods, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 6 .. 6.2
s: The baseline methods include no retrieval, single-time retrieval, previous-window retrieval, previous-sentence retrieval, and question decomposition. FLARE outperforms these methods across the reported metrics and datasets.

l: 2WikiMultihopQA, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 6 .. 6.2
s: 2WikiMultihopQA shows the largest improvement from FLARE among the evaluated tasks. On this dataset, FLAREdirect achieves 51.0 EM, 59.7 F1, 59.1 precision, and 62.6 recall, outperforming the question decomposition baseline.

l: StrategyQA, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 6 .. 6.2
s: On StrategyQA, FLARE achieves 77.3 EM, exceeding no retrieval, single-time retrieval, previous-window retrieval, and previous-sentence retrieval. Its performance drops when retrieval is activated for more than about 50% of sentences, indicating that unnecessary retrieval can introduce noise.

l: ASQA, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 6 .. 6.2
s: ASQA is described as more open-ended, making generation and evaluation more difficult. FLARE achieves the best reported results on ASQA, including 46.2 EM, 36.7 Disambig-F1, 37.7 ROUGE-L, and 37.2 DR.

l: ASQA-hint, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 6 .. 6.2
s: FLARE achieves the best reported results on ASQA-hint, with 45.9 EM, 35.7 Disambig-F1, 37.5 ROUGE-L, and 36.6 DR. The improvement over ASQA is larger because a generic hint helps language models stay on topic when ambiguous aspects are difficult to identify.

l: WikiAsp, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 6 .. 6.2
s: On WikiAsp, FLARE achieves the best reported UniEval, entity-based F1, and ROUGE-L results among the compared methods. The unit characterizes WikiAsp as an open-ended task that increases the difficulty of generation and evaluation.

l: Single-time ret., Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 6 .. 6.2
s: Single-time retrieval improves substantially over no retrieval on 2WikiMultihopQA and generally performs below FLARE. It achieves 39.4 EM and 48.8 F1 on 2WikiMultihopQA.

l: multi-time retrieval, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 6 .. 6.2
s: Multi-time retrieval methods generally outperform single-time retrieval, although their gains differ by method and dataset. The evaluated multi-time approaches include previous-window retrieval, previous-sentence retrieval, question decomposition, and FLARE.

l: Previous-window approaches, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 6 .. 6.2
s: Previous-window retrieval uses prior context to retrieve information during generation. It performs below FLARE on the reported datasets, and using more than 32 past tokens as a query hurts performance; on ASQA, it also underperforms single-time retrieval.

l: Previous-sentence approaches, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 6 .. 6.2
s: Previous-sentence retrieval retrieves using the preceding sentence and provides only a small improvement on 2WikiMultihopQA because the preceding sentence may concern different entities or relations from the next sentence. It performs worse than next-sentence retrieval on both 2WikiMultihopQA and ASQA-hint.

l: Question decomposition approaches, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 6 .. 6.2
s: Question decomposition is the strongest baseline on 2WikiMultihopQA, reaching 47.8 EM and 56.4 F1. Its manually annotated in-context examples guide language models to generate sub-questions aligned with future-generation intent, but FLARE outperforms it without requiring manual exemplar annotation.

l: confidence-based active retrieval, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 6 .. 6.2
s: Forward-looking active retrieval is presented as the central design of FLARE. Retrieving with the next sentence is clearly better than retrieving with the previous sentence, supporting the claim that future-aware retrieval is effective.

l: active retrieval, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 6 .. 6.2
s: Active retrieval selects when to retrieve using a confidence threshold. On 2WikiMultihopQA, performance plateaus when retrieval is used for more than 60% of steps, while on StrategyQA performance declines above 50%; using retrieval for roughly 40% to 80% of sentences usually performs well.

l: retrieval, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 6 .. 6.2
s: Retrieval improves results when it supplies information relevant to future generation, but unnecessary retrieval can introduce noise and impede the original generation process. Masking low-probability tokens before retrieval improves performance over retrieving with the complete sentence.

l: language model, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 6 .. 6.2
s: Language models benefit from forward-looking retrieval because it helps them access information relevant to upcoming generation. The unit also finds that generic retrieval instructions and exemplars are challenging for language models, while hints and future-oriented queries help them stay on topic.

l: Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 7
s: The unit positions FLARE within work on single-time and multi-time retrieval-augmented LMs. It distinguishes FLARE from iterative retrieval and refinement methods in text and code generation based on generation granularity and retrieval strategies. It notes that adaptive retrieval has been studied for single-time retrieval using question popularity or generation probabilities, whereas FLARE targets long-form generation requiring active information access. It also compares FLARE with browser-enhanced LMs such as WebGPT and WebCPM, noting that FLARE uses text-based retrievers but could be combined with a browser.

l: FLARE, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 7
s: FLARE differs from iterative retrieval and refinement methods in the granularity of generation and retrieval strategies. It focuses on long-form generation requiring active information access and is built on text-based retrievers, though it can potentially be combined with a browser.

l: iterative retrieval and refinement, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 7
s: Iterative retrieval and refinement has been studied in both text and code generation tasks. FLARE differs from these methods in the granularity of generation and retrieval strategies.

l: adaptive retrieval, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 7
s: Adaptive retrieval has been studied in single-time retrieval scenarios based on question popularity or generation probabilities. FLARE instead focuses on long-form generation requiring active information access.

l: long-form generation, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 7
s: Long-form generation is described as requiring active information access. FLARE focuses on this setting.

l: browser-enhanced LMs, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 7
s: Browser-enhanced LMs use browser interaction to enhance factuality, with multiple queries potentially triggered before generation. FLARE is built on text-based retrievers but can potentially be combined with a browser.

l: WebGPT, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 7
s: WebGPT trains LMs to interact with a browser to enhance factuality using reinforcement learning. Multiple queries can be triggered before generation.

l: WebCPM, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 7
s: WebCPM trains LMs to interact with a browser to enhance factuality using supervised training. Multiple queries can be triggered before generation.

l: Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 8
s: The unit concerns an active retrieval augmented generation framework for aiding long-form generation with retrieval augmentation. The framework decides when and what to retrieve during generation, using forward-looking active retrieval to identify low-confidence tokens in an upcoming sentence, retrieve relevant information, and regenerate the next sentence. Experimental results on four tasks and datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the methods. Future directions include better active retrieval strategies and efficient language model architectures for active information integration.

l: long-form generation, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 8
s: Long-form generation is aided by the proposed active retrieval augmented generation framework.

l: retrieval augmentation, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 8
s: Retrieval augmentation is used to support long-form generation through an active framework that decides when and what to retrieve during generation.

l: active retrieval augmented generation, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 8
s: The active retrieval augmented generation framework decides when and what to retrieve during generation. It is implemented with forward-looking active retrieval and is shown to be effective on four tasks and datasets.

l: confidence-based active retrieval, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 8
s: Forward-looking active retrieval iteratively uses the upcoming sentence to retrieve relevant information when the sentence contains low-confidence tokens, then regenerates the next sentence.

l: experimental results, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 8
s: Experimental results on four tasks and datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the methods.

l: future directions, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 8
s: Future directions include developing better strategies for active retrieval and efficient language model architectures for active information integration.

l: Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 9
s: The unit reports that FLARE did not provide significant gains on Wizard of Wikipedia or ELI5. Wizard of Wikipedia has relatively short outputs, while ELI5 requires long-form answers and presents grounding and evaluation difficulties. The text also notes that interleaving generation and retrieval increases computational overhead because language models must be activated multiple times and prior activations may need recomputation. Special architectures that independently encode retrieved documents and the input or generation could potentially reduce this cost.

l: FLARE, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 9
s: FLARE did not provide significant gains on Wizard of Wikipedia or ELI5. Its interleaved generation-and-retrieval approach also increases engineering and generation overhead under a naive implementation.

l: Wizard of Wikipedia, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 9
s: Wizard of Wikipedia is a knowledge-intensive dialogue generation dataset with outputs averaging approximately 20 tokens. FLARE did not provide significant gains on it, possibly because retrieving multiple disparate pieces of information is not necessary for its relatively short outputs.

l: ELI5, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 9
s: ELI5 is a long-form question-answering dataset requiring in-depth answers to open-ended questions. Neither single-time retrieval nor FLARE provided significant gains over not using retrieval, in part because of difficulties with grounding generation in retrieval and with evaluation.

l: retrieval, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 9
s: Retrieval did not provide significant gains on ELI5 when used either once or through FLARE. Interleaving retrieval with generation requires multiple language-model activations and may require recomputing previous activations in a caching-free implementation.

l: open-ended generation, Active Retrieval Augmented Generation, 9
s: Interleaving generation and retrieval increases overhead and generation cost because the language model must be activated once for each retrieval. Special architectural designs could potentially reduce this cost by independently encoding retrieved documents and the input or prior generation.

l: Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models with Iterative Retrieval-Generation Synergy, Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models with Iterative Retrieval-Generation Synergy, Abstract
s: The paper concerns ITER-RETGEN, an iterative method for retrieval-augmented generation that synergizes retrieval and generation to improve responses. It addresses limitations of large language models, including outdated knowledge and hallucinations, by using a model’s initial response to guide retrieval of more relevant knowledge. Unlike methods that interleave retrieval with generation within a single output, ITER-RETGEN processes all retrieved knowledge as a whole and preserves flexibility in generation. Evaluations on multi-hop question answering, fact verification, and commonsense reasoning show that it is superior or competitive with retrieval-augmented baselines while requiring fewer retrieval and generation operations.

l: Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models with Iterative Retrieval-Generation Synergy, Abstract
s: Retrieval-augmented generation is presented as a promising approach for addressing outdated knowledge and hallucinations in large language models. The paper improves it through the iterative retrieval-and-generation method ITER-RETGEN.

l: large language model, Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models with Iterative Retrieval-Generation Synergy, Abstract
s: Large language models are described as having limitations including outdated knowledge and hallucinations. They can be actively involved in retrieval by using generation to guide the retrieval of relevant knowledge.

l: ITER-RETGEN, Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models with Iterative Retrieval-Generation Synergy, Abstract
s: ITER-RETGEN synergizes retrieval and generation iteratively: a model’s response indicates what may be needed to complete a task, guiding retrieval of additional knowledge for a better response in a later iteration. It processes all retrieved knowledge as a whole, preserves flexibility in generation, and performs better than or competitively with retrieval-augmented baselines with fewer retrieval and generation overheads.

l: retrievers, Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models with Iterative Retrieval-Generation Synergy, Abstract
s: Retrievers struggle to capture relevance, particularly for queries involving complex information needs. ITER-RETGEN uses a model’s generated response to help retrieve more relevant knowledge.

l: non-parametric knowledge, Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models with Iterative Retrieval-Generation Synergy, Abstract
s: Retrieved knowledge is processed as a whole by ITER-RETGEN rather than being interleaved with generation under structural constraints. More relevant retrieved knowledge helps the model generate a better response in another iteration.

l: generation, Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models with Iterative Retrieval-Generation Synergy, Abstract
s: Generation provides an informative context for retrieving additional knowledge in ITER-RETGEN. The method largely preserves generation flexibility and can use both parametric and non-parametric knowledge.

l: iteration, Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models with Iterative Retrieval-Generation Synergy, Abstract
s: In each iteration, a model response can reveal what knowledge is needed to finish a task, which guides further retrieval and supports a better subsequent response.

l: multi-hop question answering, Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models with Iterative Retrieval-Generation Synergy, Abstract
s: Multi-hop question answering is one of the tasks used to evaluate ITER-RETGEN. The method is reported to perform superiorly or competitively against state-of-the-art retrieval-augmented baselines across the evaluated tasks.

l: fact verification, Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models with Iterative Retrieval-Generation Synergy, Abstract
s: Fact verification is one of the evaluation tasks for ITER-RETGEN. The results indicate that ITER-RETGEN can flexibly leverage parametric and non-parametric knowledge on the evaluated tasks.

l: commonsense reasoning, Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models with Iterative Retrieval-Generation Synergy, Abstract
s: Commonsense reasoning is included in the evaluation of ITER-RETGEN. The method achieves superior or competitive performance against state-of-the-art retrieval-augmented baselines while causing fewer retrieval and generation overheads.

l: Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models with Iterative Retrieval-Generation Synergy, Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models with Iterative Retrieval-Generation Synergy, 1
s: The unit examines how Generative Large Language Models can be improved by grounding their outputs in external knowledge. It introduces ITER-RETGEN, which iteratively combines retrieval-augmented generation with generation-augmented retrieval so that generated responses help identify additional relevant knowledge. The method is evaluated on multi-hop question answering, fact verification, and commonsense reasoning, achieving up to 8.6% absolute gains over prior retrieval-augmented methods on four of six datasets. The unit also reports that LLM-based evaluation may be more reliable than exact match and that two retrieval-generation iterations often provide the strongest gains.

l: large language model, Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models with Iterative Retrieval-Generation Synergy, 1
s: Generative Large Language Models power numerous applications but lack knowledge that is under-represented in their training data and are prone to hallucinations, especially in open-domain settings. The unit studies methods for grounding their outputs in external knowledge.

l: retrieval-augmented LMs, Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models with Iterative Retrieval-Generation Synergy, 1
s: Retrieval-augmented LMs use external knowledge to ground outputs, but previous systems typically perform one-time retrieval using only the task input. The unit proposes ITER-RETGEN as a simpler iterative alternative for tasks with complex information needs.

l: external knowledge, Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models with Iterative Retrieval-Generation Synergy, 1
s: External knowledge can potentially ground LLM outputs and reduce hallucinations. ITER-RETGEN gathers and uses additional external knowledge based on intermediate model generations.

l: open-domain question answering, Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models with Iterative Retrieval-Generation Synergy, 1
s: Open-domain question answering is identified as a setting in which LLMs are especially prone to hallucinations. The unit contrasts its complex information needs with tasks where the required information is clearly stated in the input.

l: multi-hop reasoning, Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models with Iterative Retrieval-Generation Synergy, 1
s: Multi-hop reasoning is presented as a task with complex information needs that one-time retrieval may not satisfy. ITER-RETGEN is designed to gather and process knowledge needed for such reasoning.

l: long-form question answering, Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models with Iterative Retrieval-Generation Synergy, 1
s: Long-form question answering is described as another task whose complex information needs may not be fulfilled by one-time retrieval. The unit motivates iterative retrieval-generation for this setting.

l: ITER-RETGEN, Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models with Iterative Retrieval-Generation Synergy, 1
s: ITER-RETGEN iterates retrieval-augmented generation and generation-augmented retrieval. It uses generated responses to retrieve more relevant knowledge, then uses the newly retrieved knowledge in another generation step; it achieves up to 8.6% absolute gains over previous retrieval-augmented methods on four of six datasets.

l: Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models with Iterative Retrieval-Generation Synergy, 1
s: Retrieval-augmented generation produces a response to a task input based on all retrieved knowledge, initially retrieved using the task input as the query. Within ITER-RETGEN, its output provides context for retrieving additional knowledge.

l: Generation-Augmented Retrieval, Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models with Iterative Retrieval-Generation Synergy, 1
s: Generation-augmented retrieval uses a model-generated response as informative context for retrieving more relevant knowledge. The unit also describes adapting retrieval by distilling knowledge from a re-ranker with access to model generations into a dense retriever with access only to task inputs.

l: multi-hop question answering, Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models with Iterative Retrieval-Generation Synergy, 1
s: Multi-hop question answering is one of the three tasks used to evaluate ITER-RETGEN. The method prompts an LLM to produce a chain of reasoning steps followed by a final answer and performs strongly on this type of task.

l: fact verification, Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models with Iterative Retrieval-Generation Synergy, 1
s: Fact verification is included among the tasks used to evaluate ITER-RETGEN. The introduction distinguishes single-hop fact verification as a setting where one-time retrieval may suffice.

l: commonsense reasoning, Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models with Iterative Retrieval-Generation Synergy, 1
s: Commonsense reasoning is one of the three tasks used to evaluate ITER-RETGEN. The evaluation uses few-shot prompting in which the LLM produces reasoning steps followed by the final answer.

l: natural language reasoning, Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models with Iterative Retrieval-Generation Synergy, 1
s: The method prompts an LLM to produce a chain of reasoning steps followed by the final answer. For in-context demonstrations, the authors follow Wei et al. (2022) and annotate chains of thoughts.

l: Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models with Iterative Retrieval-Generation Synergy, Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models with Iterative Retrieval-Generation Synergy, 2
s: The unit reviews limitations of LLMs, including difficult continual updating and hallucination, and describes efforts to augment them with external tools. It focuses on retrieval augmentation, contrasting passive retrieval with methods in which LLMs generate queries or other context to improve relevance. ITER-RETGEN interleaves retrieval and generation across iterations without interrupting a single generation, using prior outputs to retrieve more relevant knowledge. The unit states that ITER-RETGEN is conceptually simple and empirically strong on multi-hop question answering, fact verification, and commonsense reasoning.

l: large language model, Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models with Iterative Retrieval-Generation Synergy, 2
s: LLMs power applications such as ChatGPT, Bing Chat, and CoPilot, but they require substantial compute and data for continual updating and tend to hallucinate plausible but non-factual text. They can be augmented with tools such as code interpreters and search engines, or with retrieved information, to offload subtasks and improve their input context.

l: retrieval augmentation, Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models with Iterative Retrieval-Generation Synergy, 2
s: Retrieval augmentation connects LLMs to the external world by supplying retrieved knowledge. Earlier methods retrieved knowledge passively from task inputs, while more recent methods involve LLMs in retrieval by generating search queries, partial generations, or forward-looking sentences to improve relevance, particularly in zero-shot settings.

l: ITER-RETGEN, Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models with Iterative Retrieval-Generation Synergy, 2
s: ITER-RETGEN iterates retrieval and generation, using the complete generation from the previous iteration as specific context for retrieving more relevant knowledge in the next iteration. It avoids interrupting generation with retrieval, processes retrieved knowledge as a whole during generation, and is described as conceptually simple and empirically strong for multi-hop question answering, fact verification, and commonsense reasoning.

l: Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models with Iterative Retrieval-Generation Synergy, 2
s: Retrieval-Augmented Generation supplies generated responses with retrieved knowledge. In the example concerning the 2015 AFL Rising Star award, retrieval identifies Jesse Hogan as the winner and provides differing height information, while iterative retrieval and generation are presented as a way to improve the answer.

l: Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models with Iterative Retrieval-Generation Synergy, Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models with Iterative Retrieval-Generation Synergy, 3 / 3.1 .. 3.4
s: ITER-RETGEN is an iterative framework that repeats retrieval-generation for T iterations using a question q, a retrieval corpus D, and an LLM M. Each iteration retrieves top-k paragraphs using the previous generation and q, then generates an output using the retrieved paragraphs and q; the final output is yT. Generation-Augmented Retrieval uses previous LLM outputs to bridge semantic gaps between questions and supporting knowledge, while Retrieval-Augmented Generation prepends retrieved knowledge to q during generation. The generation-augmented retrieval adaptation further uses an LLM generation and a re-ranker to optimize the query encoder of a dense retriever through distillation.

l: ITER-RETGEN, Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models with Iterative Retrieval-Generation Synergy, 3 / 3.1 .. 3.4
s: ITER-RETGEN repeats retrieval-generation for T iterations. It uses the previous iteration's generation and the question q to retrieve paragraphs, then produces the next output with an LLM.

l: retrieval-generation, Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models with Iterative Retrieval-Generation Synergy, 3 / 3.1 .. 3.4
s: Retrieval-generation consists of retrieving top-k paragraphs using the previous generation concatenated with q, followed by prompting an LLM with the retrieved paragraphs and q. The process is repeated across iterations.

l: question q, Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models with Iterative Retrieval-Generation Synergy, 3 / 3.1 .. 3.4
s: The question q is used with the retrieval corpus to retrieve knowledge and is integrated into the LLM prompt at every iteration.

l: retrieval corpus D, Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models with Iterative Retrieval-Generation Synergy, 3 / 3.1 .. 3.4
s: The retrieval corpus D consists of paragraphs from which top-k paragraphs are retrieved during each iteration.

l: LLM M, Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models with Iterative Retrieval-Generation Synergy, 3 / 3.1 .. 3.4
s: The LLM M receives retrieved paragraphs and q in its prompt and produces an output yt at each iteration. It generates using Chain-of-Thought prompting in the described retrieval-augmented generation setup.

l: output, Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models with Iterative Retrieval-Generation Synergy, 3 / 3.1 .. 3.4
s: The output yt is generated at each iteration, with the previous output used to help retrieve paragraphs in later iterations. The last output yT is produced as the final response.

l: Generation-Augmented Retrieval, Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models with Iterative Retrieval-Generation Synergy, 3 / 3.1 .. 3.4
s: Generation-Augmented Retrieval uses the LLM output from a previous iteration to provide context for retrieval. Although the output has no guarantee of correctness, it can indicate what may be needed to answer q and help bridge semantic gaps.

l: Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models with Iterative Retrieval-Generation Synergy, 3 / 3.1 .. 3.4
s: Retrieval-Augmented Generation produces an output using Chain-of-Thought prompting while prepending retrieved knowledge to the question q. Previous generations are not incorporated directly for refinement in this setup.

l: semantic gaps, Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models with Iterative Retrieval-Generation Synergy, 3 / 3.1 .. 3.4
s: Semantic gaps can occur between the original question q and its supporting knowledge, especially when specific information needs appear only after prerequisite sub-questions are answered. A retriever with a representation bottleneck may not effectively address them.

l: retriever, Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models with Iterative Retrieval-Generation Synergy, 3 / 3.1 .. 3.4
s: The retriever retrieves paragraphs from the corpus and can have difficulty addressing semantic gaps between a question and its supporting knowledge. Its query encoder can be optimized through distillation from a re-ranker.

l: generation-augmented retrieval adaptation, Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models with Iterative Retrieval-Generation Synergy, 3 / 3.1 .. 3.4
s: The generation-augmented retrieval adaptation uses model generations to optimize the retriever so that information needs in a question can be better captured. It includes dense retrieval, a re-ranker, and distillation.

l: dense retrieval, Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models with Iterative Retrieval-Generation Synergy, 3 / 3.1 .. 3.4
s: Dense retrieval is adopted in the experiments. It represents queries and paragraphs with encoders and calculates their similarity using the inner product of their encoded vectors.

l: re-ranker, Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models with Iterative Retrieval-Generation Synergy, 3 / 3.1 .. 3.4
s: The re-ranker outputs the probability that a paragraph is relevant to a query. It is typically better at capturing query-paragraph relevance than a retriever and provides knowledge for distillation.

l: distillation, Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models with Iterative Retrieval-Generation Synergy, 3 / 3.1 .. 3.4
s: Distillation transfers knowledge from a re-ranker to a retriever. The query encoder is optimized so that the retriever's distribution conditioned on q matches the re-ranker's distribution conditioned on y1 and q using KL divergence.

l: Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models with Iterative Retrieval-Generation Synergy, Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models with Iterative Retrieval-Generation Synergy, 4 / 4.1 .. 4.7
s: The unit evaluates retrieval and reasoning methods across six datasets covering multi-hop question answering, fact verification, and commonsense reasoning. ITER-RETGEN generally outperforms or matches retrieval-augmented baselines, especially after two or more iterations, while using fewer API calls and retrieved paragraphs than ReAct and Self-Ask. The experiments show that generated reasoning can improve later retrieval, that Acc† from text-davinci-003 often better reflects semantic correctness than exact match, and that retrieval-generation synergy can correct initial factual errors. Error analysis finds that failures mainly arise from misleading first-iteration reasoning or incomplete retrieval.

l: HotPotQA, Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models with Iterative Retrieval-Generation Synergy, 4 / 4.1 .. 4.7
s: HotPotQA is used as a multi-hop question answering dataset with the October 2017 Wikipedia dump as its retrieval corpus. ITER-RETGEN reaches an Acc† of 71.2 at two iterations and 73.4 at four iterations, exceeding the retrieval-augmented baselines reported for the dataset.

l: 2WikiMultiHopQA, Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models with Iterative Retrieval-Generation Synergy, 4 / 4.1 .. 4.7
s: 2WikiMultiHopQA is evaluated as a multi-hop question answering dataset using the December 2018 Wikipedia dump. ITER-RETGEN achieves an Acc† of 58.1 at two iterations and remains competitive with Self-Ask.

l: MuSiQue, Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models with Iterative Retrieval-Generation Synergy, 4 / 4.1 .. 4.7
s: MuSiQue is evaluated using only two-hop questions, following Press et al. (2022), and uses the December 2021 Wikipedia dump for retrieval. ITER-RETGEN is competitive with Self-Ask, with an Acc† of 41.0 at two iterations.

l: Bamboogle, Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models with Iterative Retrieval-Generation Synergy, 4 / 4.1 .. 4.7
s: Bamboogle is evaluated on all 125 of its questions as a multi-hop question answering dataset. ITER-RETGEN obtains an Acc† of 59.2 at two iterations and generally outperforms the retrieval-augmented baselines.

l: Feverous, Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models with Iterative Retrieval-Generation Synergy, 4 / 4.1 .. 4.7
s: Feverous is used as the fact verification dataset and uses the December 2021 Wikipedia dump for retrieval. ITER-RETGEN is competitive with Self-Ask, reaching an Acc† of 69.5 at two iterations.

l: StrategyQA, Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models with Iterative Retrieval-Generation Synergy, 4 / 4.1 .. 4.7
s: StrategyQA is used as the commonsense reasoning dataset, with the first 500 training questions evaluated. ITER-RETGEN reaches an Acc† of 73.0 at two iterations and generally exceeds the retrieval-augmented baselines.

l: multi-hop question answering, Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models with Iterative Retrieval-Generation Synergy, 4 / 4.1 .. 4.7
s: Multi-hop question answering is one of the three evaluated reasoning tasks and includes HotPotQA, 2WikiMultiHopQA, MuSiQue, and Bamboogle. It is measured using exact match, F1, and the text-davinci-003-based Acc† metric.

l: fact verification, Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models with Iterative Retrieval-Generation Synergy, 4 / 4.1 .. 4.7
s: Fact verification is evaluated with Feverous and measured using accuracy and Acc†. The experiments find that ITER-RETGEN is competitive with the strongest baseline on this task.

l: commonsense reasoning, Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models with Iterative Retrieval-Generation Synergy, 4 / 4.1 .. 4.7
s: Commonsense reasoning is evaluated with StrategyQA using accuracy and Acc†. ITER-RETGEN generally improves over the retrieval-augmented baselines on this task.

l: Wikipedia, Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models with Iterative Retrieval-Generation Synergy, 4 / 4.1 .. 4.7
s: Wikipedia dumps provide the retrieval corpora: the October 2017 dump for HotPotQA, the December 2018 dump for 2WikiMultiHopQA, and the December 2021 dump for the other datasets.

l: ITER-RETGEN, Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models with Iterative Retrieval-Generation Synergy, 4 / 4.1 .. 4.7
s: ITER-RETGEN repeatedly performs retrieval-augmented chain-of-thought generation, using the question and previous model output to guide retrieval in later iterations. Its second iteration gives the largest typical improvement, and it often surpasses retrieval-augmented baselines with only two API calls and ten retrieved paragraphs. Its errors commonly result from incorrect first-iteration reasoning that misleads subsequent retrieval.

l: Chain-of-Thought prompting, Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models with Iterative Retrieval-Generation Synergy, 4 / 4.1 .. 4.7
s: CoT Prompting asks a model to produce natural-language reasoning steps followed by a final answer. The first iteration of ITER-RETGEN is CoT Prompting with retrieval augmentation, and both methods use the same annotated in-context demonstrations.

l: ReAct, Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models with Iterative Retrieval-Generation Synergy, 4 / 4.1 .. 4.7
s: ReAct interleaves reasoning, retrieval actions, and observations until it finalizes an answer. It is evaluated with at most five retrieval interactions and uses approximately 2.1 to 3.0 API calls and 10.6 to 15.0 retrieved paragraphs across the datasets.

l: Self-Ask, Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models with Iterative Retrieval-Generation Synergy, 4 / 4.1 .. 4.7
s: Self-Ask generates follow-up questions, retrieves information for them, and answers the follow-ups before answering the original question. ITER-RETGEN is generally more accurate or competitive while using fewer API calls and retrieved paragraphs, and it better preserves performance on questions solvable by CoT without retrieval.

l: text-davinci-003, Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models with Iterative Retrieval-Generation Synergy, 4 / 4.1 .. 4.7
s: text-davinci-003 is used as the backend language model and as an evaluator of model-output correctness through the Acc† metric. The analysis finds that Acc† more reliably identifies semantically correct answers than exact match when the two metrics disagree.

l: retrieval, Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models with Iterative Retrieval-Generation Synergy, 4 / 4.1 .. 4.7
s: Retrieval uses Contriever-MSMARCO to obtain the top five paragraphs for each query. The first iteration often has low answer recall, while later retrieval improves when it is guided by generated model output, although recall tends to plateau after the second iteration.

l: retrieval-generation synergy, Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models with Iterative Retrieval-Generation Synergy, 4 / 4.1 .. 4.7
s: Retrieval-generation synergy occurs when generated reasoning supplies phrases or concepts that help retrieve missing evidence in a later iteration. Examples show it correcting an initially wrong answer about an arena's seating capacity and an initially wrong answer about whether Raclette can be found in Paris.

l: large language model, Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models with Iterative Retrieval-Generation Synergy, 4 / 4.1 .. 4.7
s: The large language model generates reasoning, answers, search-related content, and outputs used to adapt retrieval. Its generated outputs can bridge semantic gaps between complex questions and supporting knowledge, but incorrect initial reasoning can also mislead later retrieval.

l: Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models with Iterative Retrieval-Generation Synergy, Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models with Iterative Retrieval-Generation Synergy, 5
s: Table 7 demonstrates retrieval-generation synergy through examples from HotPotQA and StrategyQA. In the first iteration, the retriever fails to find all supporting knowledge because both questions require multi-hop reasoning. Despite distractive retrieved knowledge in the HotPotQA example and imperfect parametric knowledge in the StrategyQA example, the LLM generates phrases that help retrieve relevant knowledge in the second iteration. l: Retrieval-augmented Generation across Heterogeneous Knowledge, Retrieval-augmented Generation across Heterogeneous Knowledge, Abstract
s: The unit concerns retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) methods and their use in NLP. It states that RAG methods achieve state-of-the-art performance on many NLP downstream tasks and offer easier knowledge acquisition, stronger scalability, and lower training costs than conventional pre-trained generation models. Existing RAG models have been applied to knowledge-intensive NLP tasks such as open-domain QA and dialogue systems, but most retrieve unstructured text documents from Wikipedia. The unit discusses obstacles in retrieving knowledge from a single-source homogeneous corpus and presents evidence and multiple solutions for retrieval-augmented generation across heterogeneous knowledge.

l: Retrieval-augmented Generation across Heterogeneous Knowledge, Retrieval-augmented Generation across Heterogeneous Knowledge, opening
s: The unit concerns retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) as a way to address limitations of large-scale pre-trained language models (PLMs), including stale knowledge, limited interpretability, weak domain specificity, and costly pre-training. It explains that the open-book setting augments PLM inputs with open-world resources such as encyclopedias and books, and identifies RAG as a method combining PLMs with traditional information retrieval. RAG models are described as outperforming larger PLMs on several open-domain question answering tasks while using fewer parameters, because they explicitly retrieve knowledge and generate from references. The unit argues that reliance on a single homogeneous source such as Wikipedia limits coverage and motivates retrieval across heterogeneous knowledge.

s: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) fuses pre-trained language models with traditional information retrieval techniques in the open-book setting. It has achieved state-of-the-art performance on many knowledge-intensive NLP tasks, and its knowledge is explicitly acquired through retrieval while generation is conditioned on retrieved references. The unit notes that existing RAG work has focused mainly on retrieving unstructured text from general-domain corpora and proposes studying retrieval across heterogeneous knowledge.
